new.s: Which of the following is regarded as the hallmark of the Indus Valley Civilisation?
new.x: Planned towns with grid streets, standard bricks and covered drains are the hallmark of the IVC; temples, iron and coins are not found.
new.angle: U0007 PYQ yeb1cdd885c3 IVC known for -> town planning

new.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Town planning is regarded as the hallmark of the Indus Valley Civilisation.
2. Clear remains of temples and palaces have been found in Harappan cities.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Town planning is the hallmark of the IVC, but no temples or palaces have been clearly found, unlike in Mesopotamia and Egypt.
new.angle: U0007 PYQ yeb1cdd885c3 hallmark of IVC

new.s: What was the purpose of the Great Bath at Mohenjodaro in the view of most scholars?
new.x: Most scholars see the Great Bath as a place for ritual bathing; some think it was a public tank.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT a Harappan site?
new.x: Sohgaura (Gorakhpur, UP) is known for a Mauryan-era copper plate; Sutkagendor, Desalpur and Kot Diji are Harappan sites.
new.angle: U0008 #4 Not a Harappan site -> odd-one-out

new.s: Which Harappan site is known for a series of dams feeding connected reservoirs and stepwells cut in sandstone?
new.x: Dholavira had 16 reservoirs, dams, embankments and sandstone stepwells; Mohenjodaro is known for wells and Lothal for its dock.

new.s: Which metal, the first to be used by man, did the Harappans obtain from Khetri in Rajasthan?
new.x: Copper was the first metal used by man; the Harappans got it from Khetri (Rajasthan) and Oman.
new.angle: U0009 PYQ y785cb5d52f4 first metal used by man -> copper

new.s: Which of the following metals was NOT known to the Harappans?
new.x: The Harappans used copper, bronze, gold, silver and lead, but iron has not been found; iron came only around 1000 BC.

new.s: Which of the following was a major bead-making centre of the Harappans?
new.x: Chanhudaro (with Lothal and Kalibangan) made beads of carnelian, steatite and lapis lazuli; Rohri gave chert and Kerala-no-dhoro salt.

new.s: Which of the following is a distinctive feature of the Indus Valley Civilisation and the main source on the beliefs and trade of its people?
new.x: Seals are a distinctive feature of the IVC; since the script is unread, they are the main source on the people's beliefs, animals and trade.
new.angle: U0010 #1 Seals -> value as main source

new.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Seals are a distinctive feature of the Indus Valley Civilisation.
2. As the Harappan script has been deciphered, seals are only a minor source on Harappan life.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the script is still undeciphered, so seals are the main source on the people.
new.angle: U0010 #1 Seals -> distinctive feature, value as source

new.s: In which civilisation was the lost-wax (cire perdue) technique first used in India, as seen in the bronze Dancing Girl?
new.x: The bronze Dancing Girl of Mohenjodaro was cast by the lost-wax method, so the technique was known in India from Harappan times.
new.angle: U0012 PYQ y358bc859520 lost-wax technique -> period

new.s: Which finds show that lost-wax casting continued into the Late Harappan and Chalcolithic cultures?
new.x: The Daimabad bronzes (chariot group, buffalo, rhinoceros, elephant) show that casting went on after the Mature Harappan phase.
new.angle: U0012 PYQ y358bc859520 lost-wax technique -> period

new.s: Which Harappan city had both a bead-making factory with a furnace and a shell-ornament factory?
new.x: Chanhudaro had a bead-making factory, a furnace, shell-working and bangle-making; Rakhigarhi had a gemstone factory.
new.angle: U0012 #1/#8 Bead-making and shell work -> site

new.s: Which of the following materials was NOT used by the Harappans to make beads?
new.x: Harappan beads were made of carnelian, agate, jasper, steatite, lapis lazuli, faience and gold; iron was unknown to them.

new.s: Which of the following motifs is commonly found on Harappan painted pottery?
new.x: Harappan red pottery with black designs carries geometric, floral, pipal-leaf and fish-scale motifs.
